Count the positions at which two DNA strands differ; strands of different lengths are an error.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/hamming) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: hamming.nomi
//# The Hamming distance between two DNA strands.

/// The number of positions at which two DNA strands differ. Strands of
/// different lengths have no Hamming distance.
pub fn distance(strand1: String, strand2: String) -> Result<Int, String> {
    if String.length(strand1) != String.length(strand2) {
        return Err("strands must be of equal length")
    }

    Iter.zip(strand1, strand2)
    |> Iter.filter(fn #(a, b) -> a != b)
    |> Iter.count()
    |> Ok()
}

// FILE: hamming_test.nomi
import hamming.distance

test "hamming distance" {
    cases = [
        #("empty strands", "", "", Ok(0)),
        #("single letter identical strands", "A", "A", Ok(0)),
        #("single letter different strands", "G", "T", Ok(1)),
        #("long identical strands", "GGACTGAAATCTG", "GGACTGAAATCTG", Ok(0)),
        #("long different strands", "GGACGGATTCTG", "AGGACGGATTCT", Ok(9)),
        #("disallow first strand longer", "AATG", "AAA", Err("strands must be of equal length")),
        #("disallow second strand longer", "ATA", "AGTG", Err("strands must be of equal length")),
        #("disallow empty first strand", "", "G", Err("strands must be of equal length")),
        #("disallow empty second strand", "G", "", Err("strands must be of equal length")),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, strand1, strand2, expected), description {
        assert distance(strand1, strand2) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- The result is `Result<Int, String>` with the canonical message as the
  error, rather than a one-variant error enum. There is one failure and its
  message is the useful part; an enum with a single variant would be a name
  for the same string.
- The length check is an early `return Err(...)`, and the count is a
  `zip`, `filter`, `count` pipeline ending in `|> Ok()`. Strings iterate by
  grapheme, so `Iter.zip(strand1, strand2)` pairs the letters directly.
- Every reimplemented error case uses its newest version, all with the
  message "strands must be of equal length". That leaves nine cases: five
  distances and four errors.
